source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-120: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 120 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Use a dry-run, instrumented diagnostic workflow before any mutating command or deployment change. Assume a multi-node long-context service, but do not infer platform-specific facts. Record model and runtime revisions, GPU/NIC/RDMA capabilities, PCIe/NUMA affinity, memory limits, topology and failure domains, prompt and generation-length distributions, concurrency, batching, cache warmness, and tenant policy; unresolved facts are evidence_required. This is Mooncake variant 120; distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements.

Define ownership explicitly: prefill workers construct KV and decode workers consume it. Specify block layout/schema and precision, token-position/model/revision cache keys, namespace, placement, replication, leases or epochs, version/checksum validation, TTL, eviction priority, admission quotas, and control-plane commit states. Authenticate and authorize before lookup and enforce tenant isolation. Reject stale, partial, corrupt, mismatched, or unauthorized blocks; never silently use them. For misses, RDMA timeout or link error, node loss, or control-plane inconsistency, apply bounded retry and timeout budgets, recompute locally or fall back to conventional serving, preserve correctness, fence failed owners, and record the event. Define rollback if error rate, integrity failures, fallback rate, or p99 latency breaches a predeclared threshold.

Falsifiable hypothesis: for a declared prompt-length/concurrency mix and SLO, this design reduces TTFT, inter-token or end-to-end p95/p99 latency and/or increases useful throughput versus a local-KV baseline and a conventional distributed-serving baseline without changing outputs. Measure TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency, throughput in requests/s and tokens/s, KV hit/miss rate, bytes and RDMA operations, transfer time, GPU/NIC utilization, memory occupancy, queueing, retries, fallback and error rates, with p50/p95/p99 and units. Use matched batching/load, randomized repeated trials, declared warm-up and cache state, confidence intervals, output-equivalence checks, and failure injection. Attribute RDMA separately from serialization, PCIe/NUMA copies, prefill, decode, queueing, and control-plane work. Report topology, link utilization, offered load, replication, compression/precision, competing traffic, and thermal/resource contention as confounders. Do not claim improvement until measured data and recovery evidence support it; record evidence_required and rollback observations.
risks: platform capabilities and topology may differ from assumptions
remote KV may amplify tail latency or expose stale/corrupt data without validation and fencing
failure-injection results may not generalize to production load
evidence_required: runtime/model/GPU/NIC/RDMA and topology inventory
matched local and conventional-serving benchmark data with units and repeated trials
cache hit/miss, transfer, queueing, tail-latency, correctness, and failure-recovery measurements
authorization, tenant-isolation, integrity, rollback, and node/link failure evidence
